(Forwarded internal)

Team — initial telemetry from the serving runtime and Datadog:
- P99 latency for text-generation endpoints rose from ~180ms to ~950ms between 09:05–09:20 PDT.
- Error mix: small bump in 5xx (mainly 502/504), but we also see a large burst of 499/408 patterns in our edge logs (client closed / client side timeouts).
- Traces show many incomplete server spans where the request is aborted before completion.
- Rate of incoming requests to a small set of model workers increased by ~3x briefly.

Hypothesis so far: amplification due to client SDK behavior — small client-side timeouts combined with aggressive retry settings can create a retry storm that amplifies transient latency into sustained p99 spikes. I'm pulling the QuickCommerce SDK logs (they gave us a bundle) to confirm.

Attaching a quick excerpt (logs) — filters show repeated identical request ids from the same client within seconds.

Connor

Subject: Re: Prod spike — p95/p99 regressions starting ~09:00 PDT — postmortem and next steps

Summary (root cause):
- Primary cause: client-side timeouts + aggressive retry config (QuickCommerce using redwood-js 2.4.1 with retries=6 and initial timeout 150ms) caused rapid duplicate requests when a small number of worker processes experienced transient latency.
- Amplification effect: the client retries multiplied a small transient slowdown into a burst that drove worker queueing and elevated p95/p99 across the tenant pool. Our edge logs show many requests truncated by clients (499) coincident with the retry bursts.
- Secondary contributor: our hosted default SDK/retry guidance was not prominent enough, and the SDK default policy in older 2.x releases could be misused in low-timeout environments.

What we did (mitigation):
- Immediately applied a temporary quota increase for QuickCommerce (to avoid automatic throttling) and raised the soft-concurrency guard for their tenant for the impacted window.
- We pushed a console banner and an in-product alert for customers on older SDKs recommending upgrade to redwood-js >=3.1.2 which defaults to backoff-friendly retry behavior.
- Infrastructure: added a short-term worker autoscale trigger when client 499/408 rates spike to help absorb amplification while we implement better protections.

Follow-ups (owners & ETA):
- SDK: change default retry policy to safer conservative defaults and ship a patch for 2.x maintenance branch (Connor) — ETA 2026-08-20.
- Docs/Console: surface retry guidance and an SDK health check in Console (Marissa) — ETA 2026-08-24.
- Product: Add tenant-level adaptive throttles to detect retry storms and apply coordinated backoff (Laura) — design by 2026-09-03.
- Customer: Offer a one-time credit for the impacted period and run a 30-minute post-incident call w/ QuickCommerce (Sean + Marissa) — scheduled 2026-08-18 10:00 PDT.

Customer communication draft: (to send after internal exec sign-off)
- Root cause explanation: client retry amplification + transient worker slowdown.
- Immediate mitigations we performed and recommended customer actions (upgrade SDK, adjust retry/timeouts).
- Offer credit and next steps.

Audrey — appreciate the prompt sample traces and patience. We'll send the formal postmortem and the credit proposal shortly; please let us know if the scheduled 8/18 time works.

— Sean
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
